questions.q_en: Choose the correct Active/Passive sentence.
options_en: The politician was been giving the speech.
The speech has being given by the politician.
The speech was being given by the politician.
questions.solution_en:
In Passive voice, the format is: Object of the Active voice (Subjective case) + was/were + being + V3 + by + Subject of the Active voice (Objective case).

The format of Active voice is: Subject + was/were + V1 + ing + Object.

For example:

Math was being practised by Amit. (Passive Voice)

Amit was practising Math. (Active Voice)

The options except (d) don't follow the correct grammatical format of the Passive Voice.

Therefore, the correct answer is: The speech was being given by the politician.

options_en: Sara said to her mother, "I will help Jeff and Kate."

questions.solution_en:

questions.q_en:
Select the option that expresses the given sentence in direct speech.

The Principal asked Neha where she was going after the graduation ceremony.
options_en: The Principal said to Neha, "Where you are going after the graduation ceremony?"
The Principal said to Neha, "Where have you been going after the graduation ceremony?"
The Principal said to Neha, "Where were you going after the graduation ceremony?"
The Principal said to Neha, "Where are you going after the graduation ceremony?"
questions.solution_en:
The sentence in the Indirect Speech is in Past Continuous Tense. Therefore, the sentence in the Direct Speech will be in Present Continuous Tense.

Past Continuous (Subject + was/were + V1 + ing + Object) will be converted into Present Continuous (Subject + is/am/are + V1 +ing + Object)

For example:

He said that he was checking the assignment. (Indirect Speech)

He said, "I am checking the assignment." (Direct Speech)

In the case of Interrogative sentences like this, the verb in Direct speech is always placed before the subject, unlike in Indirect Speech.

In the sentences beginning with the question word, the statement in the direct speech also begins with the same question word.

For example:

The teacher asked Jennie why she was late. (Indirect speech)

The teacher said to Jennie, "Why are you late?" (Direct speech)

The following things in the sentence will change when changed from Indirect Speech to Direct Speech:

•'She' in the indirect speech is changed into 'you' in direct speech.

•'Asked' is changed into 'said to'.

•'Was' is changed into 'are'.

Also, inverted commas ("...") are placed in direct speech.

Option (a) is eliminated because the verb 'are' is not placed before the subject 'you'. Option (b) is eliminated because it is in Present Perfect Continuous tense. Option (c) is eliminated because it is in Past Continuous tense. Option (d) is the correct answer.

The correct sentence is: The Principal said to Neha, "Where are you going after the graduation ceremony?"

questions.q_en:
Select the correct indirect form of the given sentence.

The minister said, "It is tragic that the Australian bush fires have claimed the lives of so many helpless animals."
options_en: The minister said that it was tragic that the Australian bush fires had claimed the lives of so many helpless animals.
The minister said that it was tragic that the Australian bush fires claimed the lives of so many helpless animals.
The minister said that it was tragic that the Australian bush fires were claiming the lives of so many helpless animals.
The minister said that it was tragic that the Australian bush fires have been claiming the lives of so many helpless animals.
questions.solution_en:
In the given direct speech sentence, the verb in Present tense changes to Past tense in the indirect speech sentence. The following things change in the indirect speech sentence. 'Said' remains 'said', 'said to' changes to 'told', 'has/have' becomes 'had', and 'is' becomes 'was'. Options (c) and (d) are in Past continuous and Present Perfect continuous tense respectively, but the given sentence has no continuous tense and so these options are negated. In option (b), the past tense verb 'claimed' alone is given and the verb 'have' which is given in the direct speech is left out and so this sentence is incorrect and negated. Option (a) is the correct form of the indirect speech sentence with the necessary changes that are previously mentioned.

Hence, the correct answer is option (a).

Note:

Direct and Indirect Speech: We use direct speech when we repeat someone's words and indirect speech when we use our own words to report what someone says. For Example: Direct speech: 'I like watching movies,' Seema said; Indirect speech: Seema said she likes watching movies.

One day, a very long time ago, some of the Naayire people went hunting. They walked and walked in the bush but found nothing. When night came, they were very far from home. "We must sleep in the bush," the chief said, "we must find a good place to sleep. "The hunters were not afraid to sleep in the bush. But they knew elephants, lions and other animals sometimes killed sleeping hunters. And there were some bad people, too, in the bush.

The hunters came to a place with big trees around it. They decided to rest and sleep on the grass. They did not make a fire and ate only some nuts which they carried in their bags. That was their supper. Then they went to sleep. All of them were tired. They slept soundly and did not hear anything. They did not hear that their enemies were coming nearer and nearer to them. But in one of the trees above the sleeping men, something moved and fell on the head of a young hunter. He jumped up and cried a big python was on his head!

The Naayire hunters got up quickly and saw the enemies around them. A fight began. Soon the enemies ran away and that was the end of the fight. questions.solution_en:
The subject of the Active Voice is changed into the object of the Passive Voice. Also, the object of the Active Voice is changed into the subject of the Passive Voice.

The usage of a "to be" form of the verb ['being'] is necessary while changing the voice of the sentence from Active to Passive.

In Passive Voice, the preposition "by" is used before the object. However, it is optional in some cases.

The Active voice in this question is in Present Continuous. Thus, the Passive voice will also be in Present Continuous.

The format of Active voice is: Subject + am/is/are + V1 + ing + Object.

Thus, in Passive voice, the format will be: Object of the active voice (Subjective case) + am/is/are + being + V3 + by + Subject of the active voice (Objective case).

For example:

Arnab is typing a document. (Active Voice)

questions.q_en:
Sentences of a paragraph are given below in jumbled order. Arrange the sentences in the correct order to form a meaningful and coherent paragraph.

A. This lifestyle, however, is not without its unique challenges, including navigating complex visa regulations, finding reliable internet, and combating potential loneliness.

B. Digital nomadism represents a modern lifestyle where professionals use telecommunications technologies to earn a living while conducting their lives in a nomadic manner.

C. Empowered by laptops, high-speed internet, and collaborative software, these individuals are unbound by the traditional constraints of a physical office location.

D. Consequently, they can travel the world extensively, exploring new cultures and environments while maintaining their careers and professional responsibilities from anywhere.
questions.solution_en:
Sentence B serves as the perfect introduction by defining the central concept, "Digital nomadism." Sentence C logically follows by explaining the technological enablers ("Empowered by laptops, high-speed internet...") that make this lifestyle possible for "these individuals." Sentence D builds on this by describing the consequence or the result of this empowerment, which is the ability to travel and work from anywhere. Finally, sentence A provides a concluding thought by introducing a contrast with the word "however," discussing the challenges of "This lifestyle," which aptly refers to the one described in B, C, and D. Thus, the coherent and logical order is BCDA.

Hence, option (c) is the answer.

questions.q_en:
Select the option that expresses the given sentence in reported speech.

He said, "My friend wrote me a letter."
options_en: He said that his friend had written him a letter.
He said that his friend has written him a letter.
He said that my friend had written him a letter.
He said that his friend wrote him a letter.
questions.solution_en:
The sentence in the Direct Speech is in Past Simple Tense. Therefore, the sentence in the Indirect Speech should be in Past Perfect Tense.

Past Simple (Subject + V2 + Object) should be converted into Past Perfect (Subject + had + V3 + Object).

For example:

He said, "Arya sent me a book." (Direct Speech)

He said that Arya had sent him a book. (Indirect Speech)

The following things in the sentence should change when changed from Direct speech to Indirect Speech:

"Said" will change to "said that".

"My" will change to "his".

"Wrote" will change to "had written".

"Me" will change to "him".

Therefore, the correct answer is option (a): He said that his friend had written him a letter.
